analysis.title: What we learned this week: AI Supply/Demand, Infrastructure & Financing
key_insights: GS says recent AI-ecosystem conversations focus on two questions: what the next leg of enterprise AI demand is after coding tools (and how tokens split between frontier, frontier n-1 and open-weight models), and how much financing the datacenter build-out still needs and whether credit markets are deep enough.

GS compares the recent volatility to the late Jan/early Feb software selloff: bear cases are hard to disprove and investors need time to separate out specific stocks. It views the last 4 trading days as a starting point for the market to refine its assumptions.

GS thinks the financing needed may be less than investors expect, because of BYO-hardware, vendor prepayments, cash generated by the maturing installed base, and non-traditional sources such as $19tr of private markets capital ($4.5tr of capacity to deploy per Preqin) and Nvidia's $500bn financing pool.

GS Credit Strategy benchmarks hypothetical hyperscaler issuance against the largest USD IG issuers (US banks) and estimates another $500bn of IG issuance could be supported. It warns that AI-related gross debt extends well beyond hyperscalers, so exposure concentration needs managing as the issuance cycle extends.

GS says enterprise token demand may step up again in 2027. Microsoft said the enterprise breadth motion is beginning as customers move AI into production and agents unlock consumption tied to the value of work performed.
Oracle committed to raising only $20bn of additional capital through 2030 ($10bn debt, $10bn equity). GS's data center build implied ~$65bn through 2030 and the Street estimated ~$40bn.

Oracle kept its target of adding 6GW of data center capacity through FY28. It expects total capex of ~$220bn versus GSe $180bn and Street $170bn, but is cutting its own capital burden by 50% through vendor financing of GPUs, customer bring-your-own-hardware and customer prepayments.
Oracle expects capex to fall in FY29 and FCF to turn positive in 2H28, with $30bn+ in FY29 versus GS/Street (FactSet) at $3bn/-$1bn.

Oracle's illustrative 1GW project needs ~$37bn capex, generates ~$16bn annualized revenue at full utilization, with ~35% gross margin, ~34% project-level operating margin and returns in the high 20% range. Large AI infrastructure contracts are effectively cost-plus, so hardware cost changes affect revenue and capex but largely preserve project margins and returns.

Oracle expects consolidated operating margin to trough around FY28/FY29 but stay not significantly below 40%, then reach 40%+ in FY30, as lower opex intensity offsets lower AI infrastructure gross margins.

Of Oracle's 10GW of FY28 capacity, the five flagship Stargate facilities are less than half. About 5GW comes online across all facilities between FY26 and mid FY29. Oracle delivered 850MW across ~38 projects in 11 countries in the latest quarter, with only one flagship GW-level facility (Abilene). Smaller 50-200MW deployments should matter more for distributed inference.

Microsoft launched a USD IG bond offering on Oct 29, which Bloomberg suggests could be at least $25bn. Management stressed financing flexibility (including leases), reiterated FCF positive in FY27, and discussed returns on new capex.
Microsoft capex accelerates in 2H FY (March/June 2027), partly from a ~$5bn push-out of 2QFY spending caused by third-party capacity delays.

Microsoft said it can launch capabilities comparable to leading frontier models within 3-6 months of their release at a fraction of the training cost. Azure also saw a tailwind from higher token pricing intraquarter as model releases shifted ARPU mix to the high end.
Google highlighted the release of Carbon at #1 on the Artificial Intelligence Index and said the next 12 months will bring accelerating training and launch velocity from recursive self-improvement.

GS concludes that scaling laws holding at the frontier and value accruing below the frontier (diffusion, model orchestration with dynamic routing, proprietary training on customer traces) can both be true.
GS expects the number 1 enterprise priority in 2027 to be scaling AI beyond developers. Microsoft's Foundry platform (11K models) is up 300% y/y from an undisclosed base.

GS expects CoreWeave to discuss financing at its 11/11 earnings. Its math implies ~$20bn of new debt to serve existing backlog and ~$40bn to scale to 4.2GW from 1.5GW, but no further unsecured debt or equity to ramp the 4.2GW of secured capacity.

sector_views.rationale: GS argues financing needs may be smaller than feared and IG credit markets can absorb roughly another $500bn of hyperscaler issuance, while enterprise token demand may step up in 2027.

earnings_insights: Oracle (company guidance): total capex ~$220bn vs GSe $180bn and Street $170bn; FCF positive in 2H28 and $30bn+ in FY29 vs GS $3bn and Street (FactSet) -$1bn. These are forecasts and guidance, not reported results.
Oracle (reported, latest quarter): delivered 850MW across ~38 projects in 11 countries, with one flagship GW-level facility (Abilene).

Microsoft (reported earnings commentary): guidance reiterated for FCF positive in FY27 (June 2027). 2QFY capex of ~$5bn pushed into 2HFY on third-party capacity delays. Foundry platform up 300% y/y from an undisclosed base.

CoreWeave (upcoming, 11/11 earnings, GS expectation): GS expects management to comment on financing needs. GS funding math implies ~$20bn of new debt for existing backlog and ~$40bn to reach 4.2GW from 1.5GW in 2Q.
risk_factors: AI-related gross debt extends well beyond the hyperscaler universe, so exposure concentration needs managing as the multi-year issuance cycle extends.
Third-party data center capacity delays are pushing Microsoft capex into later quarters.
Infrastructure mix puts consolidated margin pressure on Oracle, with operating margins expected to trough around FY28/FY29.
Hard-to-disprove bear cases on AI demand and financing may keep volatility elevated while investors work through specific stocks.

tension_points.bull_case: GS argues financing needs may be less than expected thanks to BYO-hardware, vendor prepayments, cash from the maturing installed base, $19tr of private markets capital and Nvidia's $500bn pool. Credit Strategy estimates the USD IG market could support another $500bn of hyperscaler issuance.
tension_points.bear_case: AI-related gross debt extends well beyond hyperscalers, so concentration of exposure becomes a risk as the multi-year issuance cycle extends. Bear cases on the build-out are described as hard to disprove.
tension_points.what_invalidates: CoreWeave's 11/11 earnings financing commentary, versus GS math showing no more unsecured debt or equity is needed to ramp its 4.2GW of secured capacity.
